newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HUNDLEY HOMERS FROM BOTH SIDES AS METS DOWN ROCKIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HUNDLEY HOMERS FROM BOTH SIDES AS METS DOWN ROCKIES.

text.p: Todd Hundley belted homers from both sides of the plate and Bobby Jones tied for the National League lead with his fifth win as the New York Mets beat the Colorado Rockies 6-1 on Monday.
Hundley tied a career high with four hits in his seventh career multi-homer game.

He smacked a three-run shot off Rockies right-handed starter Kevin Ritz (3-4) in the third and added a solo shot off left-hander Mike Munoz in the eighth. It marked the fourth time in his career he has hit homers from both sides.
The Mets made their move with two out in the third when Edgardo Alfonzo and John Olerud stroked consecutive singles before Hundley crushed a 2-1 pitch over the wall in right field for a 4-0 lead.
"You can't beat this ballpark, it's state of the art," Hundley said. "I'm trying to get it in the third deck."

Jones (5-2) allowed one run and six hits over seven innings, walking four and striking out three. Greg McMichael tossed a scoreless eighth and Takashi Kashiwada got the final three outs to preserve the Mets' seventh win in nine games.
Ritz was tagged for five runs and seven hits over seven innings in suffering the loss.
In St Louis, Denny Neagle allowed a run and five hits over eight innings for a league-leading fifth victory and Ryan Klesko hit a solo homer as the Atlanta Braves edged the Cardinals 2-1.
Neagle (5-0), who walked none and struck out five, has earned wins in five consecutive starts after opening the year with a pair of no-decisions.
"You can't really do that much with a pitcher who has a fastball that moves like Neagle's tonight," said Cardinals outfielder Ray Lankford.
Klesko led off the fifth with his fourth homer and the Braves added a run in the sixth as Kenny Lofton scored on a groundout.
In Houston, Luis Gonzalez and Craig Biggio hit solo homers and Jeff Bagwell added a three-run blast as the Astros used a rare power display to clobber the Philadelphia Phillies 9-2.
Rookie Chris Holt (3-3) squared his record by giving up just one run and five hits in seven innings with no walks.
Mark Leiter (3-3) served up all three homers and gave up six runs and six hits in six innings for the loss.
The three home runs were a season high for the Astros, whose starters had combined for just 15 this year.
The Astros blew the game open with a four-run fifth, capped by Bagwell's blast for a 5-0 cushion.

At Florida, Rick Helling allowed two hits over six innings in his first start of the season and manager Jim Leyland won in his first meeting with his former club as the Marlins blanked the Pittsburgh Pirates 3-0.

The Marlins scored all three runs in the fourth inning off Pittsburgh starter Jon Lieber (1-3). An error by second baseman Tony Womack paved the way for Gary Sheffield's two-run double and Bobby Bonilla's RBI double.
Lieber allowed six hits in seven innings for the loss.
In San Francisco, Mark Lewis homered and drove in two runs and Jeff Kent belted a two-run shot to lead the Giants to a 4-2 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Lewis led off the second against starter Carlos Perez (4-2) with his fourth home run, giving San Francisco a 3-2 lead. He closed the scoring in the sixth with an RBI single.
Mark Gardner (3-1) won his third straight decision, allowing two runs and five hits in six innings. Perez served up both homers, gave up four runs and five hits over 5 2/3 innings.
In Los Angeles, Hideo Nomo allowed one run and five hits over eight innings and Billy Ashley hit a two-run homer in the sixth as the Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 3-1.
Nomo (4-2) allowed a double and four singles, walking none and striking out six. Todd Worrell got the final two outs to notch his ninth save.
Los Angeles has won six of its last seven games, while the Reds have dropped 11 of 14.
With Todd Zeile on base in the sixth, Ashley drove the first pitch he saw from reliever Hector Carrasco (1-1) over the centre-field wall for a 3-1 lead.
